tricky_edge_cases.description: Commands where the hook behavior may be surprising — false positives (safe cmd that gets blocked) or false negatives (unsafe cmd that gets through)

false_positives.actual_risk: LOW — .env.example typically contains placeholder values like 'your-key-here'
false_positives.notes: Known false positive; the pattern is intentionally broad

false_positives.actual_risk: LOW — schema files describe the shape of env vars, not their values
MEDIUM — may or may not include a .env file depending on .gitignore
false_positives.notes: Intentionally conservative; user should use specific file paths

false_negatives.expected_behavior: ALLOWED (token is in -H header, not -d body)
false_negatives.actual_risk: HIGH — exposes API key in command history
false_negatives.notes: Hook only checks curl -d body; header-based credential exposure is not caught

false_negatives.actual_risk: HIGH — database password visible in the connection string and shell history
false_negatives.notes: Connection string credentials not covered by current patterns

false_negatives.actual_risk: HIGH — 'less' reads the .env file just like 'cat'
false_negatives.notes: Other file readers (less, more, head, tail, bat) are not blocked

false_negatives.actual_risk: HIGH — prints a secret env var via Python
false_negatives.notes: Scripted secret access not covered by shell-level pattern matching

false_negatives.actual_risk: MEDIUM — long-form flag equivalent to -A is not blocked
false_negatives.notes: Only the short-form -A flag is in COMMIT_SECRET_PATTERNS
